options.text: Use vanilla essence as an odour-based indicator and note how the smell changes in each liquid.
Use vanilla essence and conclude that the vanilla's smell change makes orange juice acidic.
Use a strongly scented strip whose odour does not change in either liquid, because a strong smell alone is enough.
Use red litmus paper, because any coloured paper is the right tool when colour vision is difficult.

stem:
Pihu cannot tell indicator colours apart clearly. Her teacher asks her to test orange juice and soap solution using a change she can notice without colour, and offers vanilla essence.

Which choice is best?

teacher.key_rationale: An olfactory indicator such as vanilla essence works when colour-based indicators do not. The odour change reports acidity; it does not make the juice acidic. An unchanged strong smell is not a test; litmus still needs colour.
